title: Multi-Region LLM Serving and KV Cache Locality

questions.question: What TTFT values does the simulator assign to a local cache hit and a cold cache miss?
questions.explanation: CACHE_HIT_MS is 80 and CACHE_MISS_MS is 800; rtt is added on top when the chosen replica is remote.

questions.question: What RTT does rtt return for an us-east-1 request served in eu-west-1?
questions.explanation: CROSSREGION_RTT includes (us-east-1, eu-west-1): 75; same-region traffic alone returns 0.

questions.question: When does GLOBAL prefer a matching remote cache over a local cold prefill?
options: Whenever the remote replica has any queue depth
Only when the remote region is eu-west-1
Never; GLOBAL always chooses a local replica
questions.explanation: GLOBAL evaluates CACHE_HIT_MS + rtt and falls back to a local replica if the best match costs more than CACHE_MISS_MS.

questions.question: Which artifact omission does the lesson identify as a 32% DR failure driver?
options: A missing GPU price list only
A missing cross-region DNS record only
An absent request ID in logs
questions.explanation: The DR checklist includes tokenizer.json/tokenizer.model and quantization configs; backing up weights alone is not enough.

questions.question: Why does ROUND_ROBIN underperform on a repeated-prefix workload?
options: It always routes all traffic to eu-west-1
It adds 800 ms of RTT to every request
questions.explanation: ROUND_ROBIN chooses replicas by index, so the same prefix is scattered across caches and many requests pay the 800 ms miss path.

questions.question: What is the key distinction between Bedrock CRI or a GKE multi-cluster gateway and the router in this lesson?
options: Commercial offerings expose KV prefix hashes to every client
The local router cannot account for RTT
The local router is only a billing API
questions.explanation: The lesson treats commercial cross-region products as opaque availability/failover, while this simulator explicitly chooses by prefix-cache state and network cost.
